questions.question: What is a distraction while driving?

options.text: Anything that makes you take quick action while driving.
Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
Anything that makes you pay more attention to driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
questions.explanation: A distraction is anything that takes your attention away from driving. Distractions can happen anywhere and anytime. Distracted driving can cause crashes that result in damage, injury, or death.

questions.question: You are driving on the freeway behind a large truck. You should:

options.text: Drive closer to the truck than you would to a regular car.
Drive farther from the truck than you would from a regular car.
Drive to the right side of the truck and wait to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive farther from the truck than you would from a regular car.
questions.explanation: Follow farther behind a large truck than you would a regular car. Large trucks have bigger blind spots where the driver cannot see you.

questions.question: When must you stop your vehicle?

options.text: When a police officer orders you to stop at an intersection.
When there is a red traffic light.
Both A and B.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both A and B.
questions.explanation: You must stop completely at a red light. You must also always follow traffic directions given by police officers, even if signs or signals say something different.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A left turn.
An upcoming stop.
A right turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: A left turn.
questions.explanation: Bicyclists use hand and arm signals because bicycles do not have turn signals. A bicyclist with their left arm straight out is signaling they will turn left.

questions.question: As daylight fades, what should you use to help others see you?

options.text: Parking lights.
Low beam headlights.
Emergency flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Turn on your low beam headlights when daylight starts to fade so others can see you. Only use high beams in open areas with no other drivers nearby.

questions.question: You see pedestrians in a crosswalk ahead. What should you do?

options.text: Continue ahead because you have the right-of-way.
Wait for the pedestrians to cross the street.
Pull to the right and drive around them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for the pedestrians to cross the street.
questions.explanation: You must let pedestrians cross at a crosswalk. Wait until the crosswalk is clear before you drive.

questions.question: If you get tired while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Stop to rest or let someone else drive.
Drink coffee.
Open a window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop to rest or let someone else drive.
questions.explanation: Stop and rest or switch drivers if you get tired. Tiredness slows your thinking and reactions, which makes driving unsafe.

questions.question: If you see a funeral procession, what must you do?

options.text: Give the right-of-way to all vehicles in the funeral procession.
You may drive between the vehicles in the procession.
You must pass the procession on the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the right-of-way to all vehicles in the funeral procession.
questions.explanation: Vehicles in a funeral procession can go through red lights. All other vehicles must give them the right-of-way, even if you have a green light, until all procession vehicles have passed.

questions.question: A driver should watch:

options.text: Straight ahead only.
Only the center of the road.
The sides, front, and back of their car.

questions.correctAnswerText: The sides, front, and back of their car.
questions.explanation: Watch all around your car. Good drivers know what is happening in all directions around their vehicle.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Bicycle crossing.
Stop only if other cars are coming.
Give the right-of-way to pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bicycle crossing.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They tell drivers that bicycles may be crossing in this area.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Dangerous intersections.
Slow-moving vehicles.
Yield signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow-moving vehicles.
questions.explanation: An orange triangle on the back of a vehicle means it moves slowly. You may see this on farm equipment, construction vehicles, or horse-drawn carriages. It looks orange during the day and red at night.

questions.question: At a crosswalk:

options.text: You must yield to pedestrians.
Pedestrians must yield to you.
Construction workers must yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must yield to pedestrians.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians have the right-of-way at crossings. You must stop for pedestrians in any crosswalk, marked or unmarked, unless a traffic signal tells them to wait.

questions.question: Reaction time is slower after:

options.text: Drinking alcohol.
Sleeping.
Working hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drinking alcohol.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reflexes and reaction time. It also reduces your vision and alertness. As you drink more, your judgment gets worse and your driving skills decrease. You will have trouble judging distances and speeds.

questions.question: If you come up behind a vehicle stopped at a crosswalk, you:

options.text: May not pass that vehicle.
Should go around the vehicle if it seems safe.
May not yield to any pedestrians in the crosswalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: May not pass that vehicle.
questions.explanation: Never pass a vehicle stopped at a crosswalk. Always yield to pedestrians when they enter the roadway.

questions.question: When turning left at an intersection:

options.text: You should always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
Oncoming traffic and pedestrians should yield to you.
You should never yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
questions.explanation: When turning left, yield to oncoming traffic traveling straight. Always yield to pedestrians.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Park your vehicle.
You are not allowed to travel in this direction.
Exit at the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are not allowed to travel in this direction.
questions.explanation: A red sign tells you that something is not allowed. This sign means you are going the wrong way. Turn around immediately.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Traffic signal ahead.
Stop.
Yield the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic signal ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a traffic signal is coming.

questions.question: Blind spots are:

options.text: Spots in your vision when you become fatigued.
Areas of the road that cannot be seen in a vehicle's mirrors.
Traffic control devices.

questions.correctAnswerText: Areas of the road that cannot be seen in a vehicle's mirrors.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. When changing lanes, look over your shoulder toward the rear corners of your vehicle.

questions.question: To prevent yourself from becoming an aggressive driver:

options.text: Relax and concentrate on driving.
Drive above the posted speed limit.
Tailgate the driver in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Relax and concentrate on driving.
questions.explanation: Concentrate on driving and don't take other drivers' actions personally. Allow enough time for your trip, follow speed limits, and be forgiving of other drivers.

questions.question: If you approach a stopped school bus that has its lights flashing and signal arm extended, you should:

options.text: Stop.
Proceed at 15 mph if no children are present.
Proceed at normal speed, but watch for children.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: Stop completely when you see a school bus with flashing lights and an extended signal arm. Stay stopped until the arm is pulled back and the bus moves. This applies whether you are behind the bus or coming from the opposite direction.

questions.question: If you drive faster than other vehicles on a two-lane road and pass many cars, what will happen?

options.text: You will reach your destination much faster and safer.
You will increase your chance of a collision.
You will help reduce traffic congestion.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will increase your chance of a collision.
questions.explanation: Do not pass other vehicles on two-lane roads. Each time you pass another vehicle, your risk of a collision goes up.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in work zones?

options.text: Follow the driver in front of you very closely.
Pass the driver in front of you as soon as possible.
Do not tailgate and keep a safe distance from other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not tailgate and keep a safe distance from other vehicles.
questions.explanation: In a work zone, keep a safe distance from traffic barriers, trucks, equipment, workers, and other vehicles. Increase your following distance and never tailgate.

questions.question: What color are traffic control devices in construction and maintenance work areas?

options.text: Red.
Orange.
Yellow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Orange.
questions.explanation: Orange signs are used in work zones. Drive with extra caution when you see orange signs, cones, or barriers on the road.

questions.question: What does tailgating (driving too close to another car's rear bumper) do?

options.text: Can anger and frustrate other drivers.
Cannot result in a traffic ticket.
Prevents other cars from cutting you off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can anger and frustrate other drivers.
questions.explanation: Tailgating is dangerous behavior that can lead to aggressive driving and should be avoided. Drivers can face legal penalties for unsafe driving.

questions.question: When you see a person crossing the street with a white cane or guide dog, what should you do?

options.text: Stop until the person is completely clear of your path.
Honk your horn and drive past them.
Carefully drive around them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until the person is completely clear of your path.
questions.explanation: When you see a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog crossing the street, you must stop until they are well away from your vehicle. Always give blind pedestrians the right-of-way.
